summary.intent: Execute all 9 plans of CipherBox phase 71 (Share-Invite Security & IPNS Data-Integrity API) via wave-based parallel subagent orchestration, then run a fully autonomous post-execution ship pipeline (verify, secure, validate, simplify, SDK E2E gate, CodeRabbit review, PR creation, review-thread resolution, learnings extraction).
summary.outcome: All 9 plans executed across 4 waves and merged with green gates (typecheck, 894/894 api tests, cargo check, sdk tests); phase verification passed 16/16. Ship pipeline completed: security/validation/simplify passed, SDK E2E gate caught and fixed a real D-05 regression (concurrent republish returning 400 instead of 409), CodeRabbit CLI findings triaged (fixes + deferred todos), PR #599 opened and pushed, a Greptile P1 (stale write key on generation-bump) and several CodeRabbit PR-review findings (write-key claim rejection, Swagger annotations, composite indexes) were fixed with matching entity/migration changes, tests re-verified (899/899), and commits were being grouped for final push when the transcript ends.

repo: cipher-box is a pnpm monorepo; root scripts define pnpm typecheck as the real cross-plan/CI-gated integration check — apps/api's own `tsc --noEmit` is NOT part of it and isn't CI-gated
GSD worktree isolation forks from live HEAD when base-check reason is 'baseref-head', allowing all waves to stay parallel without inter-wave degrade
GSD commit-tracking helper can report `commit_failed` as a false negative even when the commit lands — always verify with `git log --oneline -1`
apps/api throttling is relaxed under NODE_ENV=test, so THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET is unnecessary when the API runs in that mode

sdk-e2e (vitest) does not auto-load .env files; it falls back to SDK_E2E_SECRET default `e2e-test-secret-do-not-use-in-production` unless explicitly exported, which must match the API's TEST_LOGIN_SECRET (e2e-test-secret-ci-only) or auth 401s cascade-skip the whole suite run
packages/api-client/src/instance.ts is the place to add a temporary axios response interceptor to log err.response.data, since the API doesn't log handled 4xx responses

cipher-box repo is squash-merge only (merge:false, rebase:false, squash:true, title=PR_TITLE) — individual commit subject conventions never reach main, only the PR title needs to be conventional/paren-free

GitHub CI's Migration Drift Check only fails on structural drift (CREATE/DROP TABLE, ADD/DROP COLUMN, ALTER TYPE, RENAME COLUMN) via regex; it tolerates index/constraint name churn from `migration:generate`, so raw TypeORM migration-generate output is noisy but not indicative of a real CI failure
gh pr edit fails on this repo due to Projects-classic GraphQL incompatibility; PR body must be patched via `gh api -X PATCH repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/<N> -F body=@file`
CodeRabbit CLI review skips diffs over 150 changed files; phase 71's 106 files was under the cap
`gh pr checks` output is tab-delimited, not space-delimited — awk '{print $2}' on multi-word check names like 'CodeRabbit / Review' silently grabs the wrong field

code.finding: D-05 same-seq CID-equivocation guard threw a blanket 400 whenever embeddedSeq===dbSeq with a different CID, but this also fires for a legitimate forward-CAS attempt that lost a race (writer intended embeddedSeq=view+1, expectedSequenceNumber=view, but a concurrent writer already advanced dbSeq to embeddedSeq). Fixed by falling through to the CAS UPDATE (yielding 409) when expectedSequenceNumber === embeddedSeq-1, while preserving the 400 for true equivocation (no expectedSequenceNumber supplied).

claimInvite's widen-only merge logic (isWriteUpgrade/isGenerationBump) had a gap: when a generation bump landed on an already-write-capable share via a write-capable invite (isGenerationBump && inviteGrantsWrite but isWriteUpgrade=false), the read key/generation advanced but encryptedWriteKey stayed wrapped for the old generation, silently losing write access for the recipient post-rotation. Flagged as Greptile P1 and fixed.

Permission-derivation logic used `encryptedWriteKey !== null` which misclassifies an `undefined` write key (DTO type is string|null|undefined) as write-capable; loosened to `!= null` at both occurrences per CodeRabbit finding.

Greenfield cutover migration's down() intentionally throws (no rollback path), so composite index additions (CodeRabbit N1) only needed to be added to up() plus matching @Index decorators on share.entity.ts and share-invite.entity.ts to avoid Migration Drift Check noise.

workflow: When a subagent flags a diagnostic (e.g. rustc E0560) but reports its own check green, don't trust either blindly — settle it definitively against the merged/committed tree with the stricter check (cargo check --all-targets) before deciding it's real or stale LSP noise

For live-stack human-verify checkpoints, always verify what's actually running on the target port (stale compiled dist vs current branch code) before trusting a test run against it — a stale build can produce false negatives for the exact fix under test
When two independent reviewers (Greptile P1 + CodeRabbit MAJOR) flag the same class of issue, treat that convergence as a signal to reverse an earlier 'defer' decision rather than deferring again
Deterministic vs flaky regression triage: re-run a failing timing-sensitive test at least twice before concluding it's a real regression rather than noise

Before adding DB indexes only to a migration, check whether CI's drift check compares entities to migrated schema — matching @Index decorators are needed on the TypeORM entities or the drift check may flag noise (though ultimately this repo's drift check tolerates it)

friction: A background poll script for gh pr checks used space-based awk parsing on tab-delimited output, silently grabbing the wrong field and requiring a second corrected poll run
User had to explicitly correct the agent's assumption that CodeRabbit's review was 'skipping' — it was just slow, not skipped, causing a round of premature conclusions about review completeness

Root-cause diagnosis of the D-05 400-vs-409 regression required temporarily instrumenting packages/api-client/src/instance.ts with a debug interceptor and rebuilding the full client chain since the API doesn't log handled 4xx responses

Local DB reset (done to get a clean live-stack run for the 71-05 checkpoint) had a side effect of wiping tee_key_state, causing 2 unrelated tee-republish test failures that needed separate diagnosis to rule out as phase-71 regressions
A shell PATH glitch caused one diagnostic bash command to fail transiently and require a retry
